name: cer-ja-roundtrip
metric: round-trip CER (docs/evaluation.md §2): musculus synthesis → ruler ASR transcription → CER. Two flavours: text-level (cer_normalized, orthography noise included) and reading-level (both sides through the same ja frontend, homophone-fair phoneme comparison)

ruler.adapter: euhadra 0.3 (crates.io) ParakeetAdapter — the same model euhadra's L1 uses for ja
ruler.audio_condition: 44100 Hz decode output, FFT-resampled (rubato) to 16 kHz mono

condition.dictionary: none; JaNormalizer (built-in) active in both rows below

highlights: percent sentence fully fixed: 0.667/0.192 -> 0.000/0.000 (5パーセント spoken and heard correctly)
unit sentence now spoken メートル: reading 0.000 (text CER 0.300 is ruler writing メートル in kana vs input "m" — orthography)
date sentence reading CER 0.018 residual is ruler-side: the ASR transcribes what it hears into 年/月 kanji, and NJD reads those とし/つき — a transcription-convention floor, not a synthesis defect
coined_latin without dict is ruler-noisy (letter-reading garbled once): the dictionary closes this row (use --dict)
Wi-Fi row: ruler transcribes Latin wi-fi whose letter-reading differs from spoken ワイファイ — known ruler-noise floor (0.312)

tolerance_policy.relative: regression flag if mean reading CER exceeds 0.035 * 1.25 on the same ruler version and sentence set
tolerance_policy.absolute: mean reading CER must stay below 0.15; mean RTF must stay below 0.5 on the reference hardware (RTF varies with background load; bench_sbv2 p50 0.199 is the quiet-machine number)

notes: Reading CER is the primary intelligibility number; text CER is kept for literature comparability and to catch orthography-level drift.
The percent/date rows quantify the L3 gap worklist acoustically — ΔCER after each normalization fix lands here as a new row.
The ruler is shared with euhadra's L1 (same model + adapter), so ja CER numbers are comparable across the two projects.
Manual run only (2.4 GB ruler): cargo run --release --features onnx,wav --example eval_cer -- --json docs/benchmarks/cer-ja/run.json
